web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Forensic Audit of the Books — Cash Conversion & Capital Efficiency
question: Do IGIL's multi-year income statement, cash flows, and balance sheet confirm high-quality compounding, or are there hidden distortions from the 2024 roll-up?

epigraph.quote: Accounting profit is an opinion; cash from operations divided by EBITDA is a lie detector.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.title: Multi-year P&L trajectory and quarterly acceleration

web_blocks.html: IGIL's consolidated financial path reflects both organic scaling and the December 2024 global consolidation. Annual sales rose from ₹491 Cr in CY2022 to ₹898 Cr in CY2023 (+83% YoY) and ₹1,053 Cr in CY2024 (+17% YoY). Sales reached ₹1,598 Cr across the 15-month transition period ended March 2026 [1]. On a trailing twelve-month (TTM) basis through September 2026, revenue stands at ₹1,457 Cr (+24% YoY). TTM operating profit is ₹896 Cr (61% OPM) and net profit is ₹666 Cr [1]. Quarterly revenue rose steadily from ₹265 Cr in Dec 2024 to ₹398 Cr in Sep 2026 (+31% YoY). Quarterly net profit climbed from ₹114 Cr to ₹186 Cr (+43% YoY) over the same span [1, 5].

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Consolidated Profit & Loss Trajectory (CY2022 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating margins expanded from 55% in CY2023 to 61% in 15M FY26 and TTM Sep 2026, demonstrating strong fixed-cost leverage across global labs.

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Quarterly Performance Progression (Dec 2024 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: YoY sales growth climbed from +6% (Dec 2024) to +21% (Sep 2025, pre-GIA shift), held steady at +21% across three quarters (Sep 2025–Mar 2026), and re-accelerated post-GIA shift to +23% (Jun 2026) and +31% (Sep 2026).

web_blocks.html: The quarterly progression confirms an inflection after GIA's October 2025 policy shift. YoY sales growth climbed from +6% (Dec 2024) to +10% (Mar 2025), +16% (Jun 2025), and +21% (Sep 2025) before the rule change [1]. Growth then held steady at +21% across three quarters (Sep 2025, Dec 2025, and Mar 2026) before accelerating post-shift to +23% (Jun 2026) and +31% (Sep 2026) [1][5]. Over the same span, quarterly PAT rose from ₹114 Cr to ₹186 Cr (+43% YoY in Q2 FY27), aided modestly by a 12-quarter-low 24% effective tax rate versus the ~27% audited average (~₹6.4 Cr boost) and ₹64 Cr in TTM treasury Other Income (7.2% of ₹895 Cr PBT) [1][30]. Fixed lab costs stayed controlled as volume scaled, holding consolidated operating margins near 61% [1].

web_blocks.title: Balance sheet transformation, debt profile, and capital efficiency

web_blocks.html: Reading IGIL's balance sheet requires separating pre-IPO restructuring noise from post-IPO reality. In Dec 2023, reserves dropped to -₹605 Cr and other liabilities spiked to ₹1,484 Cr due to common-control accounting and pre-IPO promoter restructuring [1]. Following the December 2024 equity raise and the $158.2 million purchase of IGI Belgium and IGI Netherlands, equity capital rose to ₹86 Cr. Reserves rebuilt to ₹976 Cr in Dec 2024, ₹1,402 Cr in Mar 2026, and ₹1,665 Cr by Sep 2026 [1]. Total borrowings stand at just ₹150 Cr, mostly lease liabilities under Ind AS 116, against ₹1,751 Cr of shareholders' equity. The business is effectively net debt-free, earning 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE [1].

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Consolidated Balance Sheet Structure (CY2022 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Post-IPO reserves grew from ₹976 Cr (Dec 2024) to ₹1,665 Cr (Sep 2026) while borrowings remained flat at ₹150 Cr, confirming self-funded expansion.

web_blocks.title: Cash conversion and working capital forensics

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion is the strongest forensic check on IGIL's earnings quality. Pre-tax CFO/EBITDA conversion held at 87% in CY2022, 90% in CY2023, 91% in CY2024, and 94% in 15M FY26. Nearly every rupee of reported operating profit became real cash [1]. Free cash flow compounded from ₹183 Cr in CY2022 to ₹248 Cr in CY2023, ₹355 Cr in CY2024, and ₹543 Cr in 15M FY26 [1]. The ₹1,634 Cr investing outflow in CY2024 and ₹320 Cr outflow in 15M FY26 reflect the Belgium/Netherlands consolidation and the AGL buyout, not maintenance capex.

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Consolidated Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Conversion (CY2022 – 15M FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Pre-tax CFO/EBITDA conversion improved every year from 87% to 94%, generating ₹543 Cr of free cash flow in 15M FY26.

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Working Capital & Efficiency Ratios (CY2022 – 15M FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor days rose from 47 to 66 days over four periods, making receivables collection the primary forensic item to monitor.

web_blocks.html: Working-capital ratios show solid cash discipline alongside clear credit watchpoints. Inventory stays tiny because IGIL grades customer stones on consignment and holds only master reference stones [15]. Post-tax CFO/EBITDA was 64.2% in 15M FY26 (after ₹293.5 Cr in cash taxes and ₹118.7 Cr in receivables growth) versus 94.3% pre-tax [32][39]. Cash flow rebounded sharply in H1 FY27 to ₹415.7 Cr (89% of EBITDA and 118% of PAT), lifting group cash to ₹1,074.9 Cr [4][30]. Debtor days rose from 47 days in CY2022 to 66 days in 15M FY26 as large retail chains took longer credit [1]. FY2025-26 footnotes also show IGIL cut its Ind AS 109 Expected Credit Loss (ECL) allowance from ₹130.58M (7.39% in CY2024) to ₹53.48M (1.82%) [32][39]. That created a ₹53.48M provision reversal as gross receivables rose to ₹2,938.65M [32][39]. Positively, Q2 FY27 released ₹662M in receivables, pulling balances down to ₹2,402M [15][30].

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Purity, Footnote Forensics & Capital Allocation

web_blocks.html: After the December 2024 IPO and European buyout, IGIL carries zero bank debt and ₹1,074.9 Cr in cash (Sep 2026) [30]. Its 0.09x Debt/Equity stems almost wholly from Ind AS 116 lab lease liabilities [1][4]. A deeper footnote check of the FY2025-26 Annual Report and Q2 FY27 review flags four balance-sheet items to track [30][32][39]. First, post-AGL Goodwill (₹1,531.32M) and Intangibles (₹775.95M, led by AGL's ₹383.25M brand, ₹239.67M client ties, and ₹117.47M non-competes) total ₹2,307.27M, or ~13% of equity [32][39]. Second, net capex commitments sit at ₹891.76M (~₹89 Cr) after ₹82.1 Cr capex in 15M FY26 (5.1% of sales) [32][39]. Third, 11 small subsidiaries (₹1,736.35M assets, ₹178.27M Q2 revenue) were management-certified rather than auditor-reviewed in Q2 FY27 [30]. Fourth, India standalone EBITDA margin fell 340 bps YoY to 69.5% even as overseas units lifted consolidated OPM to 61.4%, and filings do not disclose standalone ex-AGL LGD fee-per-carat or commission rates [30][40].

Positively, IGIL's legal and tax profile is remarkably clean. Total contingent liabilities sit at just ₹60.76M (~₹6.1 Cr) across tax disputes (₹22.93M at CIT Appeals and ₹37.68M at CESTAT) [32][39]. The New York over-grading lawsuit by KS Trade LLC was dismissed on December 9, 2025 [32][39]. IGIL's 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE reflect an asset-light model with high asset turns. Internal cash easily funded AGL ($13.2M) and ₹5.05 per share in trailing interim dividends (₹2.50 in Feb 2026 and ₹2.55 in Aug 2026) [1][8][30].

IGIL's financial record pairs software-like margins with low fixed-asset needs and tiny contingent risk. Cash conversion stays elite across cycles, provided receivables discipline, ECL reserves, and AGL returns stay tightly governed [1][3].

book_paragraphs: A high-margin service business should leave unmistakable footprints in its cash flow statement. If profits are real, operating cash flow tracks operating profit closely, debt stays negligible, and equity compounds without repeated capital calls. IGIL passes that forensic test with room to spare—though a thorough footnote audit surfaces several subtleties that headline ratios alone obscure.

Across its audited history, revenue scaled from ₹491 Cr in CY2022 to ₹1,053 Cr in CY2024 and ₹1,598 Cr in the 15-month transition period ended March 2026. On a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026, sales reached ₹1,457 Cr with operating profit of ₹896 Cr—a 61% operating margin—and net profit of ₹666 Cr. Pre-tax operating cash flow converted 87% to 94% of operating EBITDA in every audited period (64.2% post-tax in 15M FY26 after ₹293.5 Cr cash taxes and ₹118.7 Cr receivables absorption), before surging in H1 FY27 to ₹415.7 Cr operating cash flow—89% of EBITDA and 118% of PAT—lifting group cash and bank balances to ₹1,074.9 Cr.

book_subsections.title: Cleaning the Balance Sheet Noise and Checking Credit Quality
paragraphs: At first glance, the December 2023 balance sheet looks alarming, with reserves at -₹605 Cr and other liabilities at ₹1,484 Cr. That anomaly reflects pre-IPO common-control restructuring obligations before the December 2024 listing. Once fresh IPO proceeds paid for IGI Belgium and IGI Netherlands, the balance sheet snapped into clean alignment: by September 2026, shareholders' equity reached ₹1,751 Cr (₹86 Cr share capital plus ₹1,665 Cr reserves) against zero bank debt and just ₹150 Cr of lease-driven borrowings, yielding 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE.

Forensic credit-quality checks reveal a nuanced picture. Debtor days rose from 47 days in CY2022 to 66 days in 15M FY26, and the FY2025-26 Annual Report shows management lowered its Ind AS 109 Expected Credit Loss (ECL) allowance from ₹130.58 million (7.39%) in CY2024 to ₹53.48 million (1.82%), creating a ₹53.48 million provision reversal. Encouragingly, Q2 FY27's ₹662 million receivables release validated collection velocity, while contingent tax liabilities remain tiny at ₹60.76 million and the New York Supreme Court over-grading suit by KS Trade LLC was dismissed on December 9, 2025.

book_subsections.title: Separating Real Compounding from Accounting Optics
paragraphs: Let us put the financial statements under a forensic microscope. When a company reports 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE alongside ~61% operating margins, your first instinct as a skeptic should be: is this real, or is it an artifact of accounting optics? Here, cash generation settles the core debate: H1 FY27 operating cash flow reached ₹415.7 Cr (118% of PAT) and group cash sits at ₹1,074.9 Cr. Even so, four footnotes deserve regular monitoring: combined Goodwill (₹1,531.3 million) and Intangibles (₹776.0 million, led by AGL's ₹383.3 million indefinite-life brand) now represent roughly 13% of book equity; net capital commitments reached ₹891.8 million; 11 smaller subsidiaries (₹1,736.4 million assets, ₹178.3 million Q2 revenue) were management-certified rather than auditor-reviewed in the Q2 FY27 limited review; and India standalone EBITDA margin dipped 340 bps YoY to 69.5% even as overseas subsidiaries drove consolidated leverage.

The other nuance you must account for when comparing historical periods is the fiscal-year transition. Because IGIL shifted from a December calendar year to a March fiscal year via a 15-month period ending March 31, 2026 (₹15,976M revenue), naive trailing-twelve-month comparisons can distort growth rates unless you normalize to quarterly YoY run-rates. On a clean YoY basis, Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹398.0 Cr (+31% YoY) and PAT of ₹185.8 Cr (+43% YoY) confirm that the core compounding engine is accelerating, not decelerating.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: THE MPS & ESOP OVERHANG WATCHPOINT
callouts.text: Clean cash flows do not eliminate structural share-supply risk. Blackstone still holds 76.55% as promoter ahead of SEBI's December 2027 75% cap, and Note 47 ties 60% of 19.55M ESOP 2024 options (~4.52% dilution) to Blackstone's sponsor realization milestones.

book_subsections.title: Reading the 15-Month Transition & Tax Normalization
paragraphs: Whenever a company changes its fiscal calendar, careless analysts misread the year-on-year growth table. IGIL shifted from a December year-end to an Indian March fiscal year via a 15-month period ending March 31, 2026, generating ₹15,976 million in revenue. That is why we anchor our forensic audit to both the audited CY2024 baseline and the clean three-month YoY comparisons in FY27.

Strip out the calendar noise, and the financial quality is unmistakable. Debt-to-equity sits at 0.09 times—almost entirely Ind AS 116 lease liabilities on laboratory premises rather than bank borrowings. Cash conversion remains elite, capex stood at 5.1% of sales in 15M FY26 (with ₹89.2 Cr in net capital commitments ahead), and management funded AGL's $13.2 million deal purely from internal accruals while distributing ₹5.05 per share in trailing 12-month interim dividends (₹2.50 in February 2026 and ₹2.55 in August 2026).

book_subsections.title: Cash Generation, Dividend Discipline & Return on Incremental Capital
paragraphs: Put yourself in the seat of a capital allocator looking at IGIL's balance sheet. After funding the $158.2 million Belgium and Netherlands consolidation out of IPO proceeds and paying $13.2 million in cash for AGL, IGIL still carries zero bank debt, ₹1,074.9 Cr in cash and bank balances, and generates over ₹33 of free cash flow for every ₹100 of revenue.

Because opening a new satellite lab or adding optical spectrometers requires minimal fixed capital, IGIL does not need to retain 100% of its earnings to fund 20%-plus growth. That is why the company can simultaneously invest in new capacity, fund selective bolt-on acquisitions in colored stones or rough-hub labs like IGI Botswana, and still return cash to shareholders via regular dividends while compounding ROCE near 69%.

book_subsections.title: Forensic Checklist Summary: Clean Core Cash Flows, Specific Footnote Watchpoints
paragraphs: Let us close our financial forensics chapter with an honest scorecard. Cash conversion? Elite at 87% to 94% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA and 118% OCF/PAT in H1 FY27. Leverage? Zero bank debt, with Debt/Equity at 0.09x from office leases and ₹1,074.9 Cr in cash. Legal and contingent exposure? Contained at ₹60.8 million in tax disputes following the December 2025 dismissal of the KS Trade LLC lawsuit. Return on capital? 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE.

The items on our active forensic watch-list are clear and quantifiable: receivables velocity and ECL conservatism (after ECL dropped from 7.39% to 1.82% in FY26 before Q2 FY27's ₹662 million collection release), ₹230.7 Cr of post-AGL goodwill and intangibles plus ₹89.2 Cr of capex commitments, full-year statutory audit coverage of the 11 smaller subsidiaries, India standalone margin payback (-340 bps YoY to 69.5%), and Blackstone's December 2027 MPS compliance alongside Note 47 ESOP vesting. None breaks the underlying cash-compounding engine, but all merit quarterly tracking.

book_callouts.title: What This Means for an Owner
book_callouts.text: IGIL exhibits elite core financial forensics: 61.4% consolidated operating margins, 118% OCF/PAT in H1 FY27, ₹1,074.9 Cr cash, zero bank debt, minimal ₹6.1 Cr contingent liabilities, and 69.2% ROCE. Footnote checks (ECL reduction to 1.82%, ₹230.7 Cr post-AGL goodwill/intangibles, and -340 bps India standalone margin dip) warrant ongoing tracking, while business quality retains a COMPOUNDER_PASS on price-blind fundamentals.
